concepts.definition: The speed of the music; on the card it is given as beats per minute and starts at 120.
concepts.example: At tempo 60 a 1/4 beat lasts 1000 ms; at tempo 240 it lasts 250 ms.
concepts.pitfall: Thinking the notes get longer when you raise the tempo; as the tempo goes up, the notes get shorter.

concepts.definition: A 1/4 beat lasts 60000 / tempo milliseconds; the other values are multiples of it.
concepts.example: At tempo 120 a 1/2 beat lasts 2 × 500 = 1000 ms.
concepts.pitfall: Thinking the beat value is directly in milliseconds; it is first converted using the tempo.

concepts.definition: A block that makes no sound but waits for the chosen time.
concepts.example: By putting a 1/4 beat rest between three notes, you make the rhythm clear.
concepts.pitfall: Forgetting the rests; the same notes run into each other and the rhythm is lost.

concepts.definition: Changes the speed of all the notes and rests after it; it works between 20 and 400.
concepts.example: After the set tempo to [240] block, every 1/4 beat lasts 250 ms.
concepts.pitfall: Thinking the tempo block only affects the next note; it stays in force until a new tempo block comes.

concepts.definition: A block that waits for real milliseconds; it ignores the tempo completely.
concepts.example: pause [500] ms always lasts half a second, whatever the tempo is.
concepts.pitfall: Using the pause block in a rhythm and expecting its time to change when you change the tempo.

quiz.prompt: The tempo is 60. How many milliseconds does a [1/2] beat note last? (1/4 beat = 60000 / tempo, 1/2 beat = 2 units)
quiz.explanation: At tempo 60 one unit is 60000 / 60 = 1000 ms. A 1/2 beat is two units, so it lasts 2 × 1000 = 2000 ms.

quiz.prompt: With the tempo at 240, how many milliseconds does a [1/8] beat note last? (1/8 beat = half a unit)
quiz.explanation: At tempo 240 one unit is 60000 / 240 = 250 ms. A 1/8 beat is half a unit, so it is 250 / 2 = 125 ms.

quiz.prompt:
The tempo starts at 120. When A is pressed, the program below runs. How many milliseconds do the notes take in total?

```
set tempo to [60]
play note [G] for [1/4] beat
rest for [1/4] beat
set tempo to [240]
play note [G] for [1/4] beat
rest for [1/4] beat
play note [G] for [1/4] beat
```
quiz.explanation: The first G and the first rest are 1000 ms each at tempo 60: 2000 ms. Then the tempo becomes 240; the three blocks are 250 ms each: 750 ms. Total 2000 + 750 = 2750 ms. If you think it is all at tempo 240 you get 1500; if you think it is all at tempo 60 you get 5000.

quiz.prompt:
To speed up the song, a student set the tempo to 240. The notes got shorter, but the pause after each note stayed the same:

```
set tempo to [240]
play note [C] for [1/4] beat
pause [500] ms
play note [D] for [1/4] beat
```

What is the problem?
options: The note C does not support tempo 240
The pause ms block does not listen to the tempo; a rest block should be used for the pause
The tempo block should be written twice
The note D cannot be a 1/4 beat
quiz.explanation: pause [500] ms waits for real milliseconds and does not change with the tempo. To tie the pause to the tempo, use the rest for [1/4] beat block; then the pause is 250 ms.

quiz.prompt: If you try to set the tempo to 500 in the program, what happens on the card?
options: The tempo becomes 400; the card pulls the value to the upper limit
It gives an error and the program stops
quiz.explanation: The card keeps the tempo between 20 and 400. 500 is outside the limit, so it is pulled to 400; at this speed a 1/4 beat lasts 150 ms. The program does not stop.
